effect: The arm now has feedback about muscle length, showing how the nervous system can adjust a reach as it happens.
reaction: The feedback loop was the most interesting part because it made movement feel like an ongoing process.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding position feedback was most worthwhile: it connected muscle sensing to adjustments during a reach, alongside sight.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting motor nerves to the arm felt predictable, especially as it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: I was interested to learn that the spinal cord participates in local responses, rather than serving only as a connection to the brain.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary; each had a clear role in linking sight, control, movement, or feedback.

continue.text: I would continue for another chapter to see how the body supplies and sustains the guided arm, although the sequence of mostly single available combinations offered limited choice.
